answer:
With BeautifulSoup and the `html5lib` parser: ```python from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = """
  • Django
  • Flask
""" soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html5lib") for tag in soup.find_all("li"): print(tag.sourceline, tag.sourcepos, tag.string) ``` `Tag.sourceline` is the line number where the tag was found, and `Tag.sourcepos` is its character position within that line. Beautiful Soup’s API describes both as positions in the original source document. [Beautiful Soup API](https://www.crummy.com/software/BeautifulSoup/bs4/doc/api/bs4.html) For `html5lib`, `sourcepos` refers to the position of the final `>` character of the opening tag—not the position of its initial `<`. Thus, for `
  • `, the position is `3`: ```text < l i > 0 1 2 3 ``` For example, the documented output is: ```text 6 3 Django 7 3 Flask ``` [TutorialsPoint](https://www.tutorialspoint.com/beautiful_soup/beautiful_soup_get_tag_position.htm) By contrast, `html.parser` reports the position of the initial `<`; in that parser, a tag at the beginning of a line has `sourcepos == 0`. These properties are supported by `html.parser` and `html5lib`, but not by the `lxml` parser. [TutorialsPoint](https://www.tutorialspoint.com/beautiful_soup/beautiful_soup_get_tag_position.htm) Line/position tracking can be disabled with: ```python soup = BeautifulSoup( html, "html5lib", store_line_numbers=False ) ``` In that case, `sourceline` and `sourcepos` are always `None`. [Beautiful Soup builder documentation](https://www.crummy.com/software/BeautifulSoup/bs4/doc.es/api/bs4.builder.html)
